title: Count everything the client owns
objectives: Explain why EPF, PPF, FDs, gold and property belong in the picture.
Show how hidden debt changes the equity decision.
body_md:
A client's mix is not just the money we manage. EPF, PPF, fixed deposits, gold jewellery held as savings, property and insurance-linked savings all belong in the picture, even though we do not manage them.

## Why it matters

A client with ₹25 lakh in EPF and PPF already holds a lot of debt. Counting it may mean the mutual funds can hold more equity than a standalone view would suggest. Ignoring it may mean the client is far more conservative than they intended, or far more concentrated.

## The two mistakes

- Mental accounting: "my EPF and PPF are separate, they don't count". They do; they are debt.
- Concentration: most of the wealth in the employer's shares or in one property. That belongs in the mix too.

## How to ask

"What else do you own: EPF, PPF, FDs, property, gold? Roughly how much, and when would you use it?" Then count it before suggesting any mix.
example: Arjun calls himself "100% equity", but ₹25 lakh of his ₹75 lakh total is in EPF and PPF. Counting them, his real split is about 67% equity and 33% debt — a very different conversation from the one he expected.
say: Let's count everything you own, not just the funds we manage.
Your EPF and PPF are debt, so the rest of the portfolio may be able to hold more equity.
never: Property is not part of your portfolio.
